nearFrontierPolicy.basis: Public rounded integer Intelligence Index and two-decimal USD total cost from the chart tooltips. The frontier's intelligence at a point's cost is the highest intelligence among rendered-frontier points whose cost is at or below that cost; a point cheaper than every frontier point has no gap.
nearFrontierPolicy.text: A plotted configuration is near-frontier when it lies within 3 Intelligence Index points of the rendered frontier at its cost. Every near-frontier model family must be in the primary ranking, with its own selected configuration, or be explicitly deferred with a dated, reasoned roster decision. The cost ratio to the cheapest frontier point of equal or higher intelligence is reported for information only.

barPolicy.selectionMode: deterministic at anchor freeze, before any bar outcome is computed
barPolicy.populationRule: non-provisional ranked configurations with a displayed quality
barPolicy.order: displayed quality ascending, then configuration ID
barPolicy.position: lower quartile, lower median (the headline bar) and upper quartile, each the displayed quality at zero-based position floor((n - 1) * k / 4), k = 1, 2, 3 (O34)
barPolicy.reference: the displayed quality at each ladder position, frozen as a level; the configuration at that position is recorded for audit and competes like any other
barPolicy.emptyPopulation: fewer than two population configurations: no bar pinned; the bar is published as unavailable
barPolicy.ladderPopulation: fewer than four population configurations: only the headline bar is pinned, because the quartile positions would coincide with it (E215)
barPolicy.nonTautology: a frozen level is never a configuration, so no bar can return its setter by construction; whether a result compares alternatives is published per result (possibleQualifierN, E198)
barPolicy.lifetime: fixed for the anchor version; replaced only by a versioned re-freeze that publishes old- and new-bar results on the common evaluable panel

anchorPolicy.populationRule: ranked configurations with complete cost evidence (exact cost, no AA missing- or declined-task marker) on every component of the workload at the freeze cutoff; on the main workload this is the admission reference panel
anchorPolicy.planRule: the same configurations at their displayed Plan cost: measured routes, owner-named transfers and API-cost fallbacks alike, since each is scored in the Plan table (O13, O16) and a narrower panel would clip them
anchorPolicy.belowMinimum: anchors unavailable: configurations on that workload get no cost score (the main workload must meet the minimum)
anchorPolicy.lifetime: reference IDs and costs are frozen; a population or rule change is a new anchor version with an old/new bridge, and evidence lost after freezing never rebuilds an anchor

admission.selectionRule: maximise components, then panel size, then target order, over subsets with a complete-evidence panel of at least two-thirds

assumptions: tasks are independent and each leaf's score is a mean over its published task count (plug-in binomial with the proportion (k + 1/2) / (n + 1), I28); attempts averaged within a task and tasks shared across models are ignored, so the noise is approximate
GDPval-AA: each row's rating interval as AA's model page displays it, read as a 95% normal interval (AA states no level), SD = half-width / 1.96
AA-Omniscience: each of 6,000 questions scores +1, 0 or -1, with the shares from AA's accuracy and hallucination rate
Vals boards (Vibe Code Bench v1.1, Code Migration v1.1): Vals' published standard error per record, read as the leaf's SD
AI Coding Daily: judged points over its six graded projects read as a binomial share of 60 points (an assumption; the board publishes no error)
rankSeparability.bias: net direction not established: treating two rows' errors as independent overstates the threshold, because every row is scored on the same tasks and attempts are averaged within a task; sources it omits (run-to-run and harness variance, AA's single cost run and, on the Plan basis, owner-named transfer error) work the other way
